chunks: And in the narration of Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abū Jamīlah, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Ibn Ṭarafah:
Two men claimed a camel, and each of them presented evidence, so ʿAlī عليه السلام placed it between them.

key_terms.بَعِيرًا: a camel, the disputed property in the case
key_terms.بَيِّنَةً: legal evidence or proof presented for a claim
key_terms.بَيْنَهُمَا: between the two of them, indicating division or shared assignment
key_terms.ٱدَّعَيَا: they both made a claim of ownership

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام judge when two claimants both brought evidence for the same property?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a judicial case in which two men each claimed ownership of a camel and both produced evidence. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled by assigning it between them, reflecting a legal resolution in a disputed property case when competing proofs are presented.
